stage1.impression: A calm, symmetrical living-room frame with believable plaster, a good oak floor with low raking sun stripes and a warm late-afternoon mood. The pair reads at a glance and sits at a sensible scale. The light passing through the cabinets doesn't hold together, though. The green transmitted light lands as odd flat patches (a pale vertical smear on the credenza's middle door, a hard green rectangle behind the vase) instead of a coloured pool on the floor. The cabinets glow a slightly neon lime, and the set is sparse enough that it still reads as a well-made render rather than a magazine photograph.

blocking_9: The sun visibly passes through both cabinets and throws a soft green-tinted pool onto the oak floor beside or in front of each speaker. No green light lands as a hard patch on the credenza or the wall behind the vase.
The credenza doors read as one continuous veneer, with no isolated pale vertical smear on a single door (lum_range across the doors under about 90).
Both speakers sit in comparable light, so the pair reads as a pair. Right now the left one stands against a sunlit wall (lum ~230) and the right one against shade (lum ~84).
The cover cloth reads as its true colour (delta E 2000 to #6F7F66 under 4) and not as a saturated lime green.
The speakers are grounded by a visible floor reflection or bounce of their own green, plus a contact shadow.
There is one depth layer in front of the speakers (an out-of-focus foreground element or a rug edge), so the frame stops reading as a stage flat.

defects.what: A pale yellow-green vertical light band on the credenza's middle door only, with a soft curved shadow edge. It reads as a stain or texture error, not sunlight.
A flat, hard-edged pale green rectangle on the wall behind the vase. It looks pasted on.
The vase's left side carries a lime green cast that reads like a CG emission edge.
The left cover cloth is too saturated green: RGB 91/120/88 against reference #6F7F66, delta E 5.9.
The right cover cloth is also off and brighter than the left one: RGB 109/141/106, delta E 6.6. The pair is not matched.
The wall around the right speaker is in deep shade (median 84) while the wall at the left speaker is sunlit (median 230). This creates an asymmetric pair.
The floor at the left speaker's base shows no green bounce or reflection (R 107 > G 91). The cabinet looks set down, not lit into the room.
The floor at the right speaker's base shows no green bounce or reflection (R 124 > G 99).
The cabinet interiors glow a uniform neon lime, so they read more as an emissive CG material than as sunlit tinted acrylic.
The window jamb is a wide flat cold blue-grey slab at the left edge with no texture. It is dead space in the frame.
The set is sparse and staged: a wall, a credenza and two speakers, with nothing in the foreground. There is little depth from front to back.

changes.problem: Sun through the cabinets lands as odd green patches on the credenza and wall instead of as a coloured pool on the floor, so the brief's key idea (sun passing through both cabinets) doesn't read.

evidence.measured: Credenza middle door lum_range 133.5 with a pale vertical band. A flat green patch behind the vase. The floor in front of the speakers is plain warm wood (430-1000 x 690-760: R 168, G 125, B 88).

change.to: azimuth -105 deg (from the left and slightly behind the speakers' plane), elevation 20 deg, size 0.5 deg, irradiance 55 W/m2

changes.expected: Each cabinet's shadow and transmitted green light falls forward and to the right of it on the oak floor, as a soft green-gold pool inside the frame. The credenza doors and the wall behind the vase lose their green patches.

changes.problem: The cover cloth and cabinet greens read as saturated lime, not as the specified colour.

evidence.measured: Mean RGB 91/120/88, delta E 2000 = 5.94 to #6F7F66. Right cover delta E 6.61.

change.to: 0.5 (and white_balance_k 5200 -> 5400 if the greens still read cool)

changes.expected: The covers read as a grey-green cloth and the acrylic reads as tinted glass, not neon.

changes.problem: The pair sits in unequal light: the left speaker stands against sunlit wall and the right against deep shade, so they don't read as a matched pair.

evidence.measured: Wall right of the right speaker lum_median 84.1. Wall left of the left speaker (150-230 x 100-600) lum_median 229.7.

change.to: irradiance 3.5, position [2.6, -2.8, 2.2], target [1.2, 0.6, 1.0]. This acts as a soft fill from the right so the shaded side reads as open shade, not a hole.

changes.expected: The shaded wall at the right speaker lifts to a quiet mid-tone while the sun stays clearly from the left.

changes.problem: The speakers don't ground into the floor. There is no green reflection or bounce at their bases.

evidence.measured: R 107, G 91, B 62. The floor right at the base carries none of the cabinet's colour.

changes.expected: A soft, blurred green reflection 2 to 4 cm deep under each cabinet, plus a darker contact line at the feet.

changes.problem: The frame has no foreground layer, so it reads as a flat stage set rather than a photographed room.

evidence.measured: The bottom band is empty floor. Nothing sits between the camera and the speakers.

change.to: on, position [-2.0, -2.2, 0.0], rotate 215, so only its arm and a cushion enter the lower-left corner, out of focus at f/5.6. It must not overlap the left speaker.

changes.expected: A soft-edged foreground cue in the lower-left corner adds depth and room scale while the speakers stay clear.

changes.problem: The green patch on the wall and vase reads as pasted on, because the vase sits right in the transmitted beam.

evidence.measured: A hard-edged pale green rectangle behind the vase and a lime edge on the vase's left side.

change.to: position [0.5, 0.78, 0.56] (check after c1; drop this change if c1 already clears the patch)

changes.expected: The vase reads white-warm with no green cast.

changes.problem: The left window jamb is a wide flat blue-grey slab that reads as untextured CG.

evidence.measured: A uniform cold grey with no texture, contrasting with the warm wall and the exterior.

change.to: #3E3A35 with a slight satin roughness (0.45), so it reads as powder-coated metal and recedes

changes.expected: The jamb becomes a dark, thin framing line instead of a pale slab.

out_of_scope.request: The cabinet's interior batts and ribs glow a uniform neon lime under fill light.
out_of_scope.why: That is the speaker's own material and colour. Only the light and the grade (c1, c2) may change how it reads.

out_of_scope.request: The horn measures delta E 18.4 to #4C6A36 at its lit upper edge, and its throat crushes to black (14% crush).
out_of_scope.why: The horn is part of the speaker. Its tint and the black driver throat are fixed. Light can only lift it a little.
